suite: Sample databases (Oracle CO): equivalent pairs and siblings
metric: Authored pairs on the Oracle CO schema under its declared keys, labelled equivalent or different (each 'different' label has a witness database); 13 siblings drop one key, foreign key or NOT NULL the equivalence needs. Provers: structural, algebraic/SMT with the declared constraints and its counterexample search, then the bounded checker for a counterexample.
correctness: 0 wrong: every proof also gives the same result on the real data and no proof is of a pair labelled different; every refutation's counterexample, completed with legal values, satisfies the declared constraints and separates the pair when replayed in DuckDB
held_out: 1/1 proved, 5/5 refuted, 0 wrong (a fifth of the pairs by SHA-1 of their id)
caveats: Authored pairs (52; dev 46, held out 6), not from upstream. Constraint siblings refuted: 12/13. The algebraic prover's executed counterexample search is time-limited, so on a loaded machine a refutation can fall back to unknown. No prover was changed for this eval. The first run is the baseline (nothing tuned): 18/21 proved, 28/31 refuted, 0 wrong. After the bounded checker's DATE/DATETIME fix reached master the pairs were rerun unchanged: 29/31 refuted, 0 wrong; the one pair that moved is co-window-filter-on-other-column, unknown in the baseline and refuted with a replayed database now (not isolated whether that is the fix or the search's time limit).
